nodes.label: kube-ins Desktop Application
nodes.rationale: A desktop app for managing Kubernetes clusters visually, combining a Go backend with a React/TypeScript frontend so cluster resources across multiple kubeconfigs can be inspected in one resizable panel workspace.

nodes.label: Layered Go Backend Architecture
nodes.rationale: Controller -> business -> services -> repository separation keeps Kubernetes client construction, orchestration and frontend bindings independently replaceable; it is what lets the TUI and the GUI share one business layer.

nodes.label: Controller Layer (Wails binding point)
nodes.rationale: functionBuilder.go exposes every callable method to the frontend. Bootstrap is a package-level function and start is unexported because Wails binds every exported method of App, so an exported method taking a Transport interface would break binding generation.

nodes.label: Services Layer (Kubernetes API calls)
nodes.rationale: Takes a kubernetes.Clientset as a parameter rather than using a global, so each call can be pinned to a different cluster.

nodes.label: Repository Layer (kubeconfig loading)
nodes.rationale: Two constructor families exist because per-tab panels must bypass the global active kubeconfig path; NewK8sClientForCluster loads ~/.kube-ins/{cluster}.yaml directly so a panel stays pinned regardless of the globally selected cluster.

nodes.label: IPC InstanceHub (WebSocket multi-instance discovery)
nodes.rationale: The first process binds localhost:34200 and becomes the hub server; later processes connect as clients and the hub auto-reassigns when the server exits, so no separate daemon is needed.

nodes.label: Multi-Instance Tab Transfer
nodes.rationale: Right-clicking a tab sends the panel to another running instance via TransferTab; terminal and podExec panels are excluded because live pty sessions cannot be serialized.

nodes.label: AI Assistant (Ollama tool-calling agent)
nodes.rationale: Backed by a local Ollama server so cluster data never leaves the machine. Two tool-calling modes exist because not every model advertises the native tools capability; prompt-mode replies are parsed from JSON text and never shown raw to the user.

nodes.label: AI Tool Registry (aiTools)
nodes.rationale: Single source of truth for what the model may do; mutating tools carry Mutating:true and block on a confirmation channel until the frontend approves, so the agent cannot delete resources unattended.

nodes.label: TUI / CLI Mode (tview terminal front end)
nodes.rationale: An alternative front end over the same business functions. internal/tui and cmd/tui must stay Wails-free so the CLI binary has no libwebkit2gtk/libgtk dependency.
nodes.norm_label: tui / cli mode (tview terminal front end)

nodes.label: TUI Resource Registry (buildRegistry)
nodes.rationale: Data-driven map from each view to its business.GetX/UpdateX/DeleteX functions, so a new resource is one appended resourceDef rather than a new screen.

nodes.label: Shell-Agnostic Transport Interface
nodes.rationale: Everything Wails-specific sits behind the Transport interface so functionBuilder.go and app.go contain no Wails imports; transport_wails.go is the only file in the package that imports Wails.

nodes.label: Loopback RPC Server (rpcserver.go)
nodes.rationale: A reflection dispatcher over POST /rpc/{method} that deliberately mirrors Wails promise semantics so generated bindings work unchanged. Security rests on an ephemeral loopback port, a per-process token injected into index.html rather than the URL, and an Origin check. The dispatcher wraps calls in recover because several business functions dereference a nil client after logging a construction error.

nodes.label: Shell Channel (native save dialog bridge)
nodes.rationale: Routed to the shell's main process rather than the renderer because the renderer may be reloading or crashed at that moment, and because it avoids adding a new exported App method that Wails would bind.

nodes.label: Electron Shell (shipped GUI)
nodes.rationale: Embeds Chromium so Linux packages carry no libwebkit2gtk dependency. Energy/CEF was evaluated and rejected because it merely swapped that dependency for liblcl.so plus a CEF runtime.

nodes.label: Fixed app:// Origin with protocol.handle Proxy
nodes.rationale: The sidecar binds an ephemeral port, and browser storage is keyed by origin, so loading http://127.0.0.1:<random> made every launch look like a new site and wiped persisted UI state. A fixed app:// origin proxied to the sidecar fixes this; only content-type and the token header are forwarded because passing the renderer's own headers made Chromium reject proxied module scripts with ERR_UNEXPECTED.
nodes.norm_label: fixed app:// origin with protocol.handle proxy

nodes.label: Go Sidecar Process Lifecycle
nodes.rationale: requestSingleInstanceLock is deliberately unused because multi-instance tab transfer is a feature. Shutdown is stdin.end -> SIGTERM -> SIGKILL after 3s, and serve() watches for stdin EOF so the sidecar cannot outlive a SIGKILLed Electron; the watchdog is skipped when stdin is a character device so terminal/systemd use is unaffected.

nodes.label: kubeinsdev Build Tag Relaxations
nodes.rationale: Pins the port, skips the token check (Vite serves index.html and cannot receive the injected token), and accepts loopback http origins. The origin relaxation is not optional: a Vite-served page sends Origin: http://localhost:5173 and changeOrigin rewrites Host, not Origin, so every RPC call and the /events socket would 403.

nodes.label: Wails Shell (development-only target)
nodes.rationale: Still driven by make dev/make build for debugging against the system webview, but no longer packaged: every pkg-* target and CI release job produces the Electron build.

nodes.label: electron-builder Builds, nfpm Packages
nodes.rationale: electron-builder's deb/rpm targets shell out to dpkg/fakeroot/rpmbuild which do not exist on Fedora or any non-Debian machine; nfpm is pure Go with no such dependency. Consequences: electron-builder output goes to build/electron/ so dist/ holds only shippable artifacts, chrome-sandbox must be made setuid root by a postinstall script, and artifactName is overridden because productName contains a space.

nodes.label: Per-tab Cluster Isolation
nodes.rationale: Each panel is frozen to the cluster it was opened with, so changing the global cluster via ClusterBar does not affect existing open tabs. clusterName flows from Dockview params through every layer down to NewK8sClientForCluster.

nodes.label: Panel ID Scheme
nodes.rationale: Encoding clusterName into every panel ID is what makes per-tab isolation addressable; FloatableTab must therefore prefix-match cluster-resource-view rather than compare IDs exactly.

nodes.label: Resource Triple Pattern (business/services/models)
nodes.rationale: Every core Kubernetes kind gets a parallel business/<kind>.go, services/<kind>Services.go and models/<kind>Info.go, so adding a resource is a mechanical five-step change instead of a design decision.

nodes.label: ResourceListView Shared Scaffold
nodes.rationale: Replaces ~21 hand-copied DataTable clones with one presentational shell taking a columns render-prop; only genuinely bespoke layouts (node cards, quota bars, events, monitoring) stay hand-written.

nodes.label: useResourceList Hook
nodes.rationale: Owns the fetch/poll loop, filter/selection state, multi-select delete and usePanelActive visibility gating. Effect deps are clusterName/pollInterval/active so it does not rely on remount-per-tab to pick up cluster changes.

nodes.label: usePanelActive Polling Gate
nodes.rationale: Pauses polling while a Dockview tab is backgrounded, which is why ViewPanel must thread api={api} down to each resource component.

nodes.label: Dockview Panel System
nodes.rationale: Resizable draggable panels registered by type string in DockviewContainer; sub-panels are inserted at refIndex+1 with direction 'within' so a YAML tab lands immediately right of its source panel.

nodes.label: TabInstanceBridge
nodes.rationale: A zero-render glue component that connects InstanceContext to TabContext without prop drilling.

nodes.label: Zustand Per-tab Stores
nodes.rationale: React Context holds app-wide state, but per-tab view state that must survive a tab close/reopen uses Zustand keyed by panel id. eventsStore persists to localStorage; metricsStore is the deliberately non-persisted counterpart because rolling time-series should reset on restart.

nodes.label: theme-monolith.css Variable-Driven Theming
nodes.rationale: Alternate palettes only re-bind the same CSS variables under html[data-theme], so every .p-* override automatically re-skins; adding a theme must never mean writing per-theme component rules.

nodes.label: Trivy Vulnerability Scanner Integration
nodes.rationale: Imports the Trivy library directly rather than calling the k8s API. Several non-obvious defaults are mandatory (PkgTypes, VulnSeveritySources auto, the blank modernc.org/sqlite import) or scans silently return nothing. Cluster scan is the frontend listing pod images and scanning each; there is no trivy k8s misconfig scan.

nodes.label: CRDs and Generic Object CRUD
nodes.rationale: GVR-addressed via the dynamic client rather than typed clients, so it needs the rest config. Any object is viewed/edited/deleted generically by (group, resource, namespace, name), and those same helpers are reused by the Security Role Map modal and the TUI describe panel.

nodes.label: Live Resource Monitoring Dashboard
nodes.rationale: metrics-server is point-in-time only, so trend charts are built client-side: the dashboard polls every ~4s and keeps a rolling in-memory time-series rather than asking the backend for history.

nodes.label: In-app Update Check
nodes.rationale: Fetches kubeinspector.com/version.json and compares with appVersion via semver; the manifest is generated from the git tag by the Makefile docs-downloads target and published with the site.

nodes.label: Window Screenshot (SaveSnapshot)
nodes.rationale: The frontend renders a panel to PNG via html-to-image, then Go opens a native save dialog and writes the file, because a webview a[download] is unreliable in WebKitGTK.

nodes.label: Cluster Configuration (~/.kube-ins)
nodes.rationale: Clusters are YAML files in ~/.kube-ins with the active one tracked in a .active file; both the TUI and GUI read/write that shared file so switching in CLI mode persists for the GUI.

nodes.label: GOEXPERIMENT=jsonv2 Build Requirement
nodes.rationale: Trivy pulls in encoding/json/v2, which is gated behind the jsonv2 GOEXPERIMENT on Go 1.26; the Makefile and CI export it, so bare go build/test outside make fails with a build-constraints error.

nodes.label: frontend/dist/.gitkeep Embed Bootstrap Cycle
nodes.rationale: main.go embeds frontend/dist and wails generate module parses that source, but npm run build needs the generated bindings to typecheck. The tracked placeholder breaks the cycle; /dist in .gitignore is anchored on purpose because an unanchored pattern would also match frontend/dist and git cannot re-include a file under an excluded directory.

nodes.label: wailsBridge.ts Global Shim
nodes.rationale: Supplies window.go and window.runtime backed by the RPC server rather than replacing modules, so all ~50 call sites and the generated App.js/runtime.js stay untouched. EventsOn and EventsOnce both delegate to EventsOnMultiple, so that is the method a shim must implement.

nodes.label: Event Streaming (terminal, logs, AI, tab transfer)
nodes.rationale: Backend emits via a.emit(), which reaches Wails EventsEmit or the RPC server's WebSocket depending on the shell; callback-based streaming is the shared pattern for terminal io, log tailing and AI tokens.
nodes.norm_label: event streaming (terminal, logs, ai, tab transfer)

nodes.label: Go-embedded Kubernetes JSON Schema
nodes.rationale: The schema is embedded and served over Wails as GetK8sSchema so monaco-yaml needs no external schema fetch.

nodes.label: MkDocs Documentation Site
nodes.rationale: Built with Material and deployed to Cloudflare R2 on tag push. The social plugin is gated on CI so a bare local mkdocs serve works without Cairo/Pango.

nodes.label: SEO / LLM Discoverability Files
nodes.rationale: sitemap.xml comes from the nav, robots.txt explicitly opts in AI crawlers, and llms.txt/llms-full.txt are generated by mkdocs_hooks.py so they stay in sync automatically; adding a page needs only a description front-matter.

nodes.label: Selenium + pytest E2E Suite
nodes.rationale: There are no Go unit tests; the suite drives the live dev server via Chrome, and CI spins up an ephemeral kind cluster written to ~/.kube-ins/ci.yaml.

nodes.label: Module-level DataTable Body Helpers
nodes.rationale: Defined at module scope, so clusterName must be passed as an explicit prop rather than closed over from the parent component.

nodes.label: graphify Knowledge Graph Integration (project rules)
nodes.rationale: Codebase questions should hit graphify query first because it returns a scoped subgraph, usually much smaller than GRAPH_REPORT.md or raw grep output; graphify update after code changes is AST-only and costs nothing.

nodes.label: graphify Pipeline (Steps 0-9)
nodes.source_location: What You Must Do When Invoked
nodes.rationale: Turns any folder of files into a navigable knowledge graph with community detection and an honest audit trail, producing interactive HTML, GraphRAG-ready JSON and a plain-language report.

nodes.label: Fast Path for an Existing Graph
nodes.rationale: When graph.json already exists and the request is a natural-language question, Steps 1-5 are skipped entirely and query runs immediately: the graph is already built, so re-extraction would only burn tokens.
nodes.norm_label: fast path for an existing graph

nodes.label: Python Interpreter Detection
nodes.rationale: Handles uv tool, pipx, venv and system installs by resolving an interpreter once and persisting it to .graphify_python, because under uv tool install the system python3 cannot import graphify.

nodes.label: Part A - AST Structural Extraction
nodes.rationale: Deterministic and free, requiring no LLM and no API key at all; a code-only corpus therefore skips semantic extraction entirely.

nodes.label: Part B - Semantic Extraction via Parallel Subagents
nodes.rationale: All subagents must be dispatched in a single message to run in parallel, and must be general-purpose rather than Explore, because a read-only agent cannot write chunk files and silently drops extraction results.
nodes.norm_label: part b - semantic extraction via parallel subagents

nodes.label: Semantic Extraction Cache
nodes.rationale: Cache entries are attributed to the extraction prompt file, so a graphify upgrade that changes the prompt re-extracts instead of replaying stale entries, while an unchanged prompt keeps its entries.

nodes.label: God Nodes and Surprising Connections
nodes.rationale: Surfaces the highest-degree bridge nodes and cross-community links the user would not think to ask about; these three sections are the only ones pasted into chat after a build.

nodes.label: graph.json Shrink Guard
nodes.rationale: to_json refuses to write when the new graph has fewer nodes than the existing one, and the report plus analysis sidecar are only written when the graph actually was, so they never describe a graph graph.json does not contain.

nodes.label: Graph Health Check (integrity gate)
nodes.rationale: Read-only and never aborts, but surfaces edge collapse, dangling/missing endpoints and self-loops - the silent-corruption modes of incremental updates and AST/LLM id mismatches.

nodes.label: Honesty Rules
nodes.rationale: Never invent an edge, never hide cohesion behind symbols, always show token cost - the audit trail is the product, so uncertainty must be labeled rather than smoothed over.

nodes.label: No API Key Required Policy
nodes.rationale: graphify reads only GEMINI_API_KEY/GOOGLE_API_KEY and never ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or OPENAI_API_KEY; when no Gemini key is set the host agent itself is the LLM, so prompting for or blocking on a key is a misread of the skill.

nodes.label: EXTRACTED/INFERRED/AMBIGUOUS Confidence Rubric
nodes.rationale: Discrete values (0.95/0.85/0.75/0.65/0.55) replace a continuous range because models follow discrete rubrics better; production showed the range being collapsed into a bimodal binary with over half the edges parked at 0.5.

nodes.label: Deterministic Node ID Format
nodes.rationale: IDs use the full repo-relative path stem so same-named files in different directories stay distinct and semantic IDs match the AST extractor's; chunk or sequence suffixes are forbidden because the same entity must produce the same ID regardless of which chunk processes it.

nodes.label: Verbatim source_file Rule
nodes.rationale: Copying the FILE_LIST path character-for-character keeps the full build and incremental --update on the same base, so build_merge's replace-on-re-extract matches the existing node instead of accumulating a duplicate.

nodes.label: Hyperedges
nodes.rationale: Used only when three or more nodes participate in a shared flow that pairwise edges do not capture, capped at three per chunk to keep them informative.

nodes.label: semantically_similar_to Edges
nodes.rationale: Connects concepts that solve the same problem with no structural link at all - the edges a purely structural extractor can never find.

nodes.label: Rationale as Node Attribute
nodes.rationale: Design intent and trade-offs are stored on the relevant concept node rather than as separate rationale or fragment nodes, so only genuine named entities become nodes.

nodes.label: Call Edge Direction and Language Rule
nodes.rationale: Source must be the caller and target the callee, and calls edges must stay within one language, because cross-language call edges are phantom artifacts.
nodes.norm_label: call edge direction and language rule

nodes.label: Constrained Query Expansion
nodes.rationale: The matcher does case-folded substring plus IDF with no stemming, synonyms or cross-language matching, so a vocabulary mismatch returns zero hits and the answer collapses to noise. Expansion must draw only from the graph's own extracted vocabulary, never from training memory.

nodes.label: BFS Traversal Mode
nodes.rationale: Default mode, depth 3, for broad context questions like 'what is X connected to'.

nodes.label: DFS Traversal Mode
nodes.rationale: Depth-limited to 6 to avoid traversing the whole graph; used to trace a specific dependency chain rather than gather neighbors.

nodes.label: Token-Budget-Aware Output
nodes.rationale: Nodes are ranked by term relevance and the output is cut at roughly four characters per token, so the most relevant context survives truncation.

nodes.label: Work Memory / Self-Improving Loop
nodes.rationale: save-result with an outcome records preferred sources, known dead ends and corrections into LESSONS.md, so future sessions skip paths that already led nowhere. reflect --if-stale makes reading them nearly free.

nodes.label: Incremental --update Flow
nodes.rationale: Re-extracts only new or changed files to save tokens and time; detect_incremental splits the corpus into a changed subset and the full file list so downstream steps see both.

nodes.label: build_merge Replace-on-Re-extract
nodes.rationale: Reads graph.json directly without a NetworkX round-trip so edge direction is preserved. prune_sources is only for genuinely deleted files - adding changed files there would delete the freshly re-extracted content, since replace-on-re-extract already drops every re-extracted source_file from the base.

nodes.label: Code-Only Update Fast Path
nodes.rationale: When every changed file is code, semantic extraction is skipped entirely and no LLM is needed - only AST runs.

nodes.label: --cluster-only Reclustering
nodes.rationale: Self-contained: it regenerates report, graph.json and html from the existing graph. Steps 5-9 must not be re-run because they read intermediate files a prior build's cleanup already deleted.

nodes.label: Portable Relative Manifest
nodes.rationale: Manifest keys are relativized to the scan root so they stay portable across clones and machines; without it a moved project makes --update miss every cached file.

nodes.label: Neo4j Export
nodes.rationale: Uses MERGE so re-running never creates duplicates.

nodes.label: FalkorDB Export
nodes.rationale: Statements are OpenCypher, but FalkorDB's GRAPH.QUERY runs one statement at a time with no bulk script import, so pushing directly is preferred over generating cypher.txt.

nodes.label: Agent-Crawlable Wiki Export
nodes.rationale: Must run before Step 9 cleanup while .graphify_labels.json still exists.

nodes.label: MCP stdio Server
nodes.rationale: Exposes query_graph, get_node, get_neighbors, get_community, god_nodes, graph_stats and shortest_path so other agents can query the graph live. Claude Desktop config must use the absolute interpreter path because it cannot run command substitution and the system python3 may not import graphify.

nodes.label: Token Reduction Benchmark
nodes.rationale: Runs only above 5,000 words because for small corpora the graph's value is structural clarity, not token compression.

nodes.label: Post-Commit Auto-Rebuild Hook
nodes.rationale: Triggers once per commit instead of running a background process, works with any editor, and appends to an existing post-commit hook rather than replacing it. Doc and image changes are ignored and need a manual --update.

nodes.label: Native CLAUDE.md Integration
nodes.rationale: Writes a graphify section into the project CLAUDE.md so the graph is consulted automatically in future sessions with no manual /graphify.

nodes.label: URL Ingest (/graphify add)
nodes.rationale: Auto-detects YouTube, Twitter/X, arXiv, PDF, image and generic webpage URLs, saves them into the corpus, then runs the --update pipeline to merge the new file into the existing graph.

nodes.label: Folder Watcher (--watch)
nodes.rationale: Code changes rebuild immediately with no LLM; docs/papers/images only set a needs_update flag. Debouncing exists so a wave of parallel agent writes does not trigger one rebuild per file.

nodes.label: Whisper Video/Audio Transcription
nodes.rationale: The agent composes the Whisper initial prompt itself from existing god-node labels rather than making a separate API call, which improves domain-term accuracy. Transcript paths are written from Python instead of a shell redirect because Whisper prints progress to stdout and would corrupt the JSON.

nodes.label: GitHub Repo Clone
nodes.rationale: Clones into ~/.graphify/repos/<owner>/<repo> and reuses existing clones on repeat runs.

nodes.label: Cross-Repo / Monorepo Graph Merge
nodes.rationale: The skill pipeline always writes to graphify-out/ in the cwd, so running it per subfolder would clobber the same output dir; the CLI is used per subfolder instead because it places graphify-out/ inside the scanned path. Each merged node keeps a repo attribute for filtering by origin.

nodes.label: SIL Open Font License v1.1
nodes.rationale: Permits free use, study, modification and redistribution of the fonts, but forbids selling the font software by itself and requires that modified versions carry a different reserved name.
